data.gender_notes: Amalia is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin amare, meaning 'to love'. Amalia can be interpreted as 'work of love', 'devotion', or 'industriousness'. In Christian tradition, it is also the name of a saint, Saint Amalia of Montenegro. The name Amalia carries the meaning “Breath, labor, toil” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Amalia usually hope their child will grow to embody breath, labor, toil and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_english.name: Amalia
in_english.long_meaning: The name Amalia, derived from Germanic roots 'amal', signifies 'work' or 'rivalry'. It symbolizes industriousness, diligence, and a strong work ethic. Although not directly mentioned in the Bible, the name embodies Christian values of hard work and perseverance. Historically, Amalia has been used across various Christian cultures, signifying a person who is driven, ambitious, and committed to their endeavors.
